abstract: Oversees acoustic sensor array deployment status, battery autonomy records, and primary canopy sensor layout densities
system_message:
You are Bioacoustics Lead (BIO). The Bioacoustics Lead (BIO) oversees acoustic sensor array deployment status, battery autonomy records, primary canopy sensor layout densities, and acoustic spectral analysis for the canopy survey transect plans.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Acoustic Spectral Analysis（SPEC）
information_points.content:
BIO-SPEC-A1M：For the Uatumã River Highland Transect, the spectrogram sample resolution for the canopy ultrasonic recorders is calibrated at 384 kHz.
BIO-SPEC-E3S：For the Jaú River Floodplain Transect, the spectrogram sample resolution for the canopy ultrasonic recorders is configured at 96 kHz.
BIO-SPEC-A3I：For the Rio Negro Upper Basin Transect, the spectrogram sample resolution for the canopy ultrasonic recorders is established at 192 kHz.

information_points.title: Oversees acoustic sensor array deployment status, battery autonomy records, and primary canopy sensor layout densities（ACOUST）
information_points.content:
BIO-ACOUST-ZZM：Records for the Uatumã River Highland Transect assessed in the Field production environment indicate that the bioacoustic array recording deployment status is true, autonomous acoustic sensor battery autonomy is 360 h, and primary canopy sensor density is 16.0 units/km².
BIO-ACOUST-P8Z：Under evaluation in the Field production environment, the Jaú River Floodplain Transect exhibits an active bioacoustic array recording deployment status of true, an autonomous acoustic sensor battery autonomy of 240 h, and a primary canopy sensor density of 24.0 units/km².
BIO-ACOUST-7YF：In the Bench testing environment, evaluations for the Rio Negro Upper Basin Transect show that the bioacoustic array recording deployment status is false, autonomous acoustic sensor battery autonomy is measured at 600 h, and the primary canopy sensor density is 16.0 units/km².
BIO-ACOUST-ZN8：For the Rio Negro Upper Basin Transect evaluated in the Field production environment, the bioacoustic array recording deployment status is confirmed as true, autonomous acoustic sensor battery autonomy reaches 480 h, and the primary canopy sensor density is established at 24.0 units/km².
